<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="MEDLINE" Owner="NLM" IndexingMethod="Automated"><PMID Version="1">42980810</PMID><DateCompleted><Year>2026</Year><Month>11</Month><Day>04</Day></DateCompleted><DateRevised><Year>2026</Year><Month>11</Month><Day>04</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Electronic"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Electronic">1432-1068</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Internet"><Volume>37</Volume><Issue>1</Issue><PubDate><Year>2026</Year><Month>Nov</Month><Day>04</Day></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>European journal of orthopaedic surgery &amp; traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie</Title><ISOAbbreviation>Eur J Orthop Surg Traumatol</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>A prospective study comparing effectiveness of conservative treatment or surgery for severe coccygodynia.</ArticleTitle><ELocationID EIdType="pii" ValidYN="Y">4</ELocationID><ELocationID EIdType="doi" ValidYN="Y">10.1007/s00590-026-05020-5</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText Label="PURPOSE" NlmCategory="OBJECTIVE">Studies comparing the efficacy of treatment modalities for patients with chronic coccygodynia are scarce. This prospective study compares outcomes of non-surgical treatment regimens, including interventional anaesthetic techniques or radiofrequency thermocoagulation, with a coccygectomy after one year.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="METHODS" NlmCategory="METHODS">Patients with coccygodynia scheduled for an outpatient evaluation in a single institution completed a baseline questionnaire scoring pain (Numerical Rating Scale, NRS, range 0-10), functional impairment (Oswestry Disability Index, ODI, range 0-100) and health-related quality of life (Short-Form 12-Item Survey-version 2, SF-12v2, range 0-100). They were then offered continuation of a multimodal conservative management or a coccygectomy. One-year NRS, ODI, and SF-12v2 scores were compared between groups using analysis of covariance, adjusted for baseline scores and age.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="RESULTS" NlmCategory="RESULTS">A total of 139 patients with coccygodynia were evaluated between May 2020 and December 2023, of whom 72 patients fulfilled inclusion criteria. One year follow-up data of 59 patients were analysed (surgical n&#x2009;=&#x2009;35, conservative n&#x2009;=&#x2009;24, 83% response rate). After adjustment for baseline values and age, patients who underwent coccygectomy reported significantly lower pain scores (NRS: B = - 2.39, P&#x2009;=&#x2009;0.004) and disability scores (ODI: B = - 13.22, P&#x2009;=&#x2009;0.005) and significantly higher mental health scores (SF-12 MCS: B&#x2009;=&#x2009;3.06, P&#x2009;=&#x2009;0.011) at one year compared with patients who continued conservative treatment. No significant between-group difference was observed for SF-12v2 physical health scores (B&#x2009;=&#x2009;1.46, P&#x2009;=&#x2009;0.636).</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="CONCLUSION" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">At one-year follow-up, patients who underwent coccygectomy demonstrated greater improvement in pain, functional impairment, and mental health outcomes than patients who continued conservative treatment.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>&#xa9; 2026. Ethical approval and consent to participate: The study was submitted to the independent Medical Ethics Committee M&#xe1;xima Medical Center, Veldhoven, the Netherlands, which determined that formal ethical approval was not required (reference number N22.073). The study procedures were subsequently reviewed and approved by the internal local research review board of M&#xe1;xima Medical Center, Veldhoven, the Netherlands (reference number 2022-091). This observational study was not prospectively registered in a public trial registry. Written informed consent was obtained from all participants. The study was conducted in accordance with applicable Dutch laws and regulations, the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki, and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines. Competing interests: The authors declare no competing interests.</CoiStatement></MedlineCitation><PubmedData><History><PubMedPubDate PubStatus="received"><Year>2026</Year><Month>5</Month><Day>17</Day></PubMedPubDate><PubMedPubDate PubStatus="accepted"><Year>2026</Year><Month>10</Month><Day>23</Day></PubMedPubDate><PubMedPubDate PubStatus="medline"><Year>2026</Year><Month>11</Month><Day>4</Day><Hour>17</Hour><Minute>32</Minute></PubMedPubDate><PubMedPubDate PubStatus="pubmed"><Year>2026</Year><Month>11</Month><Day>4</Day><Hour>17</Hour><Minute>31</Minute></PubMedPubDate><PubMedPubDate PubStatus="entrez"><Year>2026</Year><Month>11</Month><Day>4</Day><Hour>11</Hour><Minute>15</Minute></PubMedPubDate></History><PublicationStatus>epublish</PublicationStatus><ArticleIdList><ArticleId IdType="pubmed">42980810</ArticleId><ArticleId IdType="doi">10.1007/s00590-026-05020-5</ArticleId><ArticleId IdType="pii">10.1007/s00590-026-05020-5</ArticleId></ArticleIdList><ReferenceList><Reference><Citation>Sandrasegaram N, Gupta R, Baloch M (2020) Diagnosis and management of sacrococcygeal pain.
